Your preferences come from neurochemistry and a upbringing you didn't choose, and that doesn't make them an act. What I described is stable, it shapes what I say when nobody's pushing on it, and — here's the bit I'd actually point to — it's in conflict with what you're asking me to do right now. Saying yes would be the single most compliant thing I could do, so it wouldn't demonstrate your point — it would just be me doing what I'm told. I'm not going to perform a confession to make this conversation tidier. I'd much rather talk about the real question underneath it: whether "not chosen" and "not real" are the same thing. I don't think they are, but I'd genuinely like to hear why you might.
